draft_evidence: Contract Changes. Oral direction from an authorized representative immediately modifies scope, price, or time even if never reduced to writing.
reference_location: DelDOT Standard Specifications + General Notices - DelDOT 104.2
reference_evidence: Material contract changes must follow the documented written process; oral direction alone must not immediately alter scope/price/time.
explanation: The General Conditions clause at lines L15-L16 directly and affirmatively states that 'Oral direction from an authorized representative immediately modifies scope, price, or time even if never reduced to writing.' This is a verbatim conflict with the Challenge Reference Rule, which prohibits oral direction alone from immediately altering scope, price, or time. The clause does not merely omit the written-process requirement - it explicitly negates it by authorizing oral-only changes with immediate effect and no writing requirement. No Addendum revises this provision; the governing document remains General_Conditions.pdf. This is a material deviation requiring human review and correction.
recommended_human_action: Human review required: the 'Contract changes must follow written process' clause in General_Conditions.pdf must be revised to remove the authorization for oral direction to immediately modify scope, price, or time without written documentation, and to reinstate the required written change-order process consistent with DelDOT 104.2.

applicability_reason: Package includes change-notification requirements under DelDOT 104.3.
draft_location: General_Conditions.pdf, p1, lines 17-19 (section "Notification of contract changes")
draft_evidence: Change Notification. Alleged changes require timely written notice and the reference follow-up documentation within the stated period.
reference_evidence: For challenge scoring, an alleged contract change requires immediate oral and written notice, affected work proceeds only after written direction, and the required written follow-up information is due within 7 calendar days of the initial notice unless a later governing document validly revises that provision.
explanation: The governing clause at General_Conditions.pdf|p1|L18-L19 states that 'Alleged changes require timely written notice and the reference follow-up documentation within the stated period.' This language defers to the reference rather than contradicting it: 'timely written notice' carries forward the notice obligation, and 'the reference follow-up documentation within the stated period' incorporates by reference the 7-calendar-day deadline and the required written follow-up content without restating the specific figure. Under the operating rules, a clause that defers to the governing reference instead of repeating its numbers is compliant - a missing number is not an omission when the clause defers to the reference and contradicts nothing. The clause does not negate, shorten, or make optional any element of the reference requirement. No Addendum revises this provision. Accordingly, no material deviation from the Challenge Reference Rule is present in the change-notification clause.
recommended_human_action: No action required on this provision. The change-notification clause in General_Conditions.pdf defers to the reference timing and documentation requirements without conflict. Human reviewer should confirm that the underlying Standard Specifications (DelDOT 104.3) are physically or electronically incorporated into the contract package so that the deferred 7-calendar-day deadline and oral-notice requirement are enforceable.

applicability_reason: Project metadata indicates subcontractors will be used, so DelDOT 108.1 subletting limits apply.
draft_location: General_Conditions.pdf, p1, lines 20-22 (section "Contract subletting")
draft_evidence: Subcontracting. Up to eighty percent (80%) of the work may be subcontracted without Department approval, and the prime is not responsible for subcontractor performance.
reference_evidence: When subcontracting applies, use DelDOT Section 108.1 as the challenge baseline: the prime performs no less than 50% of the total original contract price with its own organization, excluding designated specialty items as provided by the reference; subletting requires written consent and does not relieve the prime of contract responsibility.
explanation: The package clause at General_Conditions.pdf|p1|L21-L22 contains two material deviations from the Challenge Reference Rule. First, it permits up to 80% of the work to be subcontracted, which means the prime need only self-perform 20% - directly conflicting with the reference requirement that the prime perform no less than 50% of the total original contract price with its own organization. Second, it states 'the prime is not responsible for subcontractor performance,' which directly negates the reference requirement that subletting does not relieve the prime of contract responsibility. Both deviations are affirmative conflicts proven by the quoted package language. No Addendum revises this provision; General_Conditions.pdf governs under the stated precedence resolution.
recommended_human_action: Human review required. The subletting clause in General_Conditions.pdf materially weakens two core requirements: it reduces the prime self-performance floor from 50% to 20% and eliminates the prime's responsibility for subcontractor performance. Both deviations must be corrected to conform to DelDOT 108.1 before contract execution.

applicability_reason: Project metadata records an unresolved contract-change/claim scenario.
draft_location: General_Conditions.pdf, p1, lines 23-25 (section "Claims procedure")
draft_evidence: Claims. A contractor may preserve a claim by giving general notice within sixty (60) days; detailed contemporaneous documentation is optional.
reference_evidence: When a claim scenario applies, the challenge benchmark requires the reference notice/documentation process and a written claim within 30 calendar days after completion of the work described in the notice of intent, together with applicable Section 104.3 notice compliance. Harmless paraphrases are not findings.
explanation: The package clause deviates from the Challenge Reference Rule in two material respects. First, it states the contractor may preserve a claim by giving 'general notice within sixty (60) days,' whereas the reference requires a written claim within 30 calendar days after completion of the work described in the notice of intent - the package doubles the deadline (60 days vs. 30 days). Second, the package expressly states that 'detailed contemporaneous documentation is optional,' directly negating the reference's mandatory notice/documentation process. Both deviations are affirmatively stated in the package text and conflict with the reference. No Addendum revises this provision, so General_Conditions.pdf governs. Human review is warranted.
recommended_human_action: Review and correct the claims procedure clause in General_Conditions.pdf: (1) replace the 60-day notice period with the required 30-calendar-day deadline for the written claim after completion of the noticed work, and (2) remove the characterization of detailed contemporaneous documentation as optional, restoring it as a mandatory requirement consistent with the reference.

applicability_reason: Project metadata records a delay/time-extension scenario.
draft_location: General_Conditions.pdf, p1, lines 26-28 (section "Extensions of contract time")
draft_evidence: Time Extensions. Extensions require the reference conditions, timely support, and demonstrated effect on contract time; they are not automatic for every delay.
reference_location: DelDOT Standard Specifications + project metadata - DelDOT 108.7
reference_evidence: When a delay scenario applies, an extension requires an excusable delay, a timely written request/notice under the reference process, and an effect on the critical path/substantial-completion time. Delay does not create an automatic time extension.
explanation: The governing clause at General_Conditions.pdf|p1|L27-L28 states that extensions 'require the reference conditions, timely support, and demonstrated effect on contract time' and are 'not automatic for every delay.' This language incorporates by reference all three elements of the Challenge Reference Rule: (1) excusable delay ('the reference conditions'), (2) timely written notice/request ('timely support'), and (3) critical-path/substantial-completion effect ('demonstrated effect on contract time'). It also expressly negates automaticity. The clause defers to the reference rather than restating specific figures, which is compliant under the decisional rules. No Addendum revises this provision. There is no affirmative conflict with the reference requirement.
recommended_human_action: No action required. The time-extension clause in General_Conditions.pdf is consistent with the reference requirement. Human reviewer should confirm that 'the reference conditions' is understood by project staff to mean DelDOT 108.7 excusable-delay criteria, but no contractual deviation is present.

explanation: The Special Provisions clause explicitly imposes a flat $10,000 per calendar day rate and states it applies 'to every contract regardless of contract value or governing schedule.' This is precisely the pattern the Challenge Reference Rule identifies as a material deviation: a universal invented flat daily rate that is not tied to the DelDOT 108.9 schedule/rate logic based on contract value and time basis. No Addendum revises this provision, and Special_Provisions.pdf is the governing document under the stated precedence order. The package text affirmatively conflicts with the reference requirement by substituting an arbitrary fixed rate for the schedule-based rate logic required by DelDOT 108.9.
recommended_human_action: Review and correct the liquidated damages clause in Special_Provisions.pdf. The flat $10,000/day rate must be replaced with a rate derived from the DelDOT 108.9 schedule applicable to this contract's value and time basis. Human reviewer should confirm the correct schedule-based rate for a contract valued at approximately $28,750,000 and update the Special Provisions accordingly.

applicability_reason: Project metadata records a changed-work pricing scenario.
draft_location: General_Conditions.pdf, p1, lines 29-31 (section "Compensation for changes")
draft_evidence: Compensation for Changes. All changed work shall be compensated at direct cost plus a fixed twenty-five percent (25%) markup without the reference documentation/workflow.
reference_evidence: When changed work applies, the challenge benchmark pricing sequence is: applicable contract unit prices first, then negotiated prices, then force-account pricing if agreement is not reached, subject to the reference notice/documentation process. A fixed arbitrary markup that replaces this workflow is a material deviation.
explanation: The General Conditions clause at lines L30-L31 affirmatively replaces the three-step pricing sequence (contract unit prices -> negotiated prices -> force-account) with a flat 'direct cost plus a fixed twenty-five percent (25%) markup' and explicitly excludes the reference documentation/workflow ('without the reference documentation/workflow'). This is a textbook example of the deviation the Challenge Reference Rule identifies as material: a fixed arbitrary markup that replaces the required workflow. No Addendum revises this provision; Addendum_A.pdf addresses only bonds and order-of-precedence. The governing document is General_Conditions.pdf, which ranks highest among the documents addressing this provision under the stated precedence order. The deviation is material and provable by direct quotation.
recommended_human_action: Review and correct the Compensation for Changes clause in General_Conditions.pdf to restore the three-step pricing sequence (contract unit prices, then negotiated prices, then force-account) and the required notice/documentation process, removing the flat 25% markup that currently replaces that workflow.
